articles.title: Not glamorous, but common: how to manage dandruff at home and when to get help
articles.summary: Experts don’t know exactly what causes dandruff, but if you’re seeing light flakes on your scalp, over-the-counter products can help. You spy a scatter of white flakes on your collar. Or you’ve got an itch that won’t quit, no matter how much you wash your hair.
body: An itchy, flaking scalp is rarely dangerous, but it can be annoying. Here’s what you need to know about what might be causing your flakes, what you can do about it, and when it’s time to get help.

Dandruff is the mildest form of a condition called seborrheic dermatitis, a type of skin inflammation that usually affects the head, face or trunk. At its worst, this condition leads to patches of red skin covered in tiny, greasy scales. However, most people with dandruff have just minor scaliness and no redness, affecting only the scalp.

Experts still don’t know exactly what causes dandruff, and it’s likely there are various contributing factors. A yeast called Malassezia is a leading suspect, says James Pathoulas, an assistant professor of dermatology at the University of Minnesota medical school who specializes in hair and scalp disorders. Malassezia usually lives harmlessly on the scalp, but overgrowth has been linked with scalp inflammation.
points: Experts don’t know exactly what causes dandruff, but if you’re seeing light flakes on your scalp, over-the-counter products can help.

articles.title: My deep fryer lives in a tool polycule. Here’s how to stop buying things your friends already own
articles.summary: The key to happiness isn’t hoarding gadgets – it’s loaning them out and buying fewer things. Sign up for the Filter US newsletter, your weekly guide to buying fewer, better things.
body: They live under your bed and in your basement, your garage and probably in that weird cabinet above the fridge that requires a stepstool.

Alton Brown calls them unitaskers: the tools and appliances that aspire to do only one thing and do it well. Pasta makers and juicers are the classics, but they exist outside the kitchen, too. Do you really need to own a post-hole digger? Seasonal candle molds?

Well yes, sometimes. Which is why so many of us have them lurking in the recesses of our homes and apartments, gathering dust while they wait for the next dinner party that requires homemade ravioli. Local tool libraries solve this problem for home projects by filling shelves with borrowable tools instead of books. But if you don’t have one near you, or just tasks beyond DIY, I have a solution anyone can try: start a tool polycule.

For years now, half a dozen friends and I have operated an informal group here in Portland, Oregon, that swaps all the insipid items that spend 364 days a year sitting unused. It’s less a library than a group of people taking a nonmonogamous view of products instead of partners (though that type of polycule is popular in Portland, too).
points: The key to happiness isn’t hoarding gadgets – it’s loaning them out and buying fewer things.

articles.title: Mytheresa and Chloë Sevigny—and a Best-Dressed Crowd—Brought New York Style to the Forefront
articles.summary: There was no better incentive for folks to get extra dressed-up than Mytheresa’s signature fashion-filled cocktail party—particularly because of its prime Saturday night slot on the calendar.
body: Switching things up, this time it unfolded in Café Chelsea at the fabled Hotel Chelsea—the French Art Deco bistro making for a fitting setting for a night that always fuses Euro elegance with effortless New York style.

On hosting duty, actress and muse Chloë Sevigny showed why she’s maintained her status as the city’s coolest girl (since before quote-unquote cool girls were a thing) in a fur-adorned, thigh-skimming brocade mini by Saint Laurent. It made for a meta moment. The fashion plate is currently starring in Mytheresa’s Fall 2026 campaign, with the front cover image of the print zine shot on the balcony of this very hotel. Around the space, Sevigny’s face beamed back from postcards and mailers everywhere you looked.

Whether people stopped by before or after their dinner plans, the room was buzzing with front row faces from start to finish. After all, if the Europeans are in town—New Yorkers know how to show them a good time.
points: There was no better incentive for folks to get extra dressed-up than Mytheresa’s signature fashion-filled cocktail party—particularly because of its prime Saturday night slot on the calendar.

articles.title: Elkie Brooks looks back: ‘Before I went on stage I used to drink Guinness and a few shots of brandy’
articles.summary: The singer-songwriter on her rock’n’roll past, playing second fiddle to the Beatles, and the key to being an energetic performer in your 80s. Born Elaine Bookbinder in Salford in 1945, Elkie Brooks is a rock, blues and jazz singer known as the British Queen of Blues.
body: This is me in a white jumpsuit outside the Royal Albert Hall in London. I have very few memories of the gig, but I know I would have felt daunted as it’s such a large venue. To overcome the nerves, I’d have tried to focus on the music and remembered, “It’s just another gig.”

Ever since I can remember, I have been singing, often in the bath, to my mummy. When I was seven I would get invited to sing Mr Sandman with the band that would play at weddings and barmitzvahs. As I got older, I adored Johnnie Ray and Ella Fitzgerald, then Billie Holiday, Sarah Vaughan, Dakota Staton, Esther Phillips and Aretha Franklin. The cantor at the local synagogue used to give me singing lessons, all in Hebrew and Yiddish. He was the one who taught me the correct way to project my voice.

articles.title: Veronica Beard Gathered Trailblazers for a Golden Hour Toast to Fall 2026
articles.summary: As the sun set over downtown New York City, guests banded together to honor the women who inspired them and pay tribute to the tragedies of 9/11.
body: “We are always celebrating women,” Swanson Beard told Vogue. “Every woman is our muse, every season. We constantly talk about iconic women, trailblazers, and women who lit the way for us in every field. We also talk about the trailblazer at home. A mother is a trailblazer. A woman in her community making a difference is a trailblazer. There’s so many levels and variations of trailblazers—but it’s all women doing amazing things.”

Of course, plenty of trailblazing women were also in attendance. Serena Williams arrived in a velvet suit by the label, while Pamela Anderson made a surprise appearance in a bandana-style silk dress. Zoey Deutch, Apple Martin, former WNBA star Lisa Leslie, and scientist Keiana Cave also mingled with smoky Palomas and Champagne in hand. “They told me I was the ultimate trailblazer,” Williams told Vogue. “I was like, ‘No way, but thank you for saying that.’ To hear that from them, the Veronicas, was really cool.”

articles.title: Alexandra Leclerc Gets a Little Extra (Extra!) at the Spanish Grand Prix
articles.summary: The art historian, model, dog mom, and F1 WAG is the latest star to don the Dior by John Galliano newspaper print dress.
body: Some dresses will live forever: Princess Diana’s revenge dress is one, a Dior by John Galliano newspaper print slip another. It’s the latter, seen on Alexandra Leclerc, that edged it this week.

The day before, Leclerc was in her home of Monaco to celebrate the launch of her Rhode collab, opting for a sugary, sparkly pink midi dress to reflect her shimmering line of products. (All named for her world: the ‘Monaco’ and ‘Gemini’ Pocket Blushes included.) Clearly, Leclerc loves a statement-making dress moment.

Paddock fashion has come to be defined by modern F1 WAGs like Alexandra Leclerc (who married Charles in February, and is reported to be pregnant with their first child): across the last few weeks she’s kept to her floaty, feminine aesthetic codes, playing with homegrown brands and luxury accessories. At the Italian Grand Prix, she wore a polka-dot Marelea halter dress and fire-red Ferrari gown. In Madrid, she opted for Spanish label Desigual’s pink flocked halter dress and a slinky black Silvia Tcherassi co-ord.

articles.title: Powered by Matcha and Hometown Spirit, Hayes Warner Hypes up Kaia Gerber at Khaite
articles.summary: It was a homecoming twice-over for New York-raised Hayes Warner, who sat front row of Khaite’s spring 2027 show, which was opened by her “The Shards” co-star.
body: Hayes Warner has wasted no time getting reacquainted with a New York minute. Back in her hometown after a whirlwind trip to Venice Film Festival, the Los Angeles-based, New York-raised actor has thrown herself straight into the NYFW party circuit, taken her place on the front rows alongside Chloë Sevigny and other stars-of-the-moment, and even carved out time for a trip to the U.S. Open. “Gorgeous clothes. Gorgeous people. Gorgeous food. Gorgeous life,” is how she sums up the week.

Her trip to Khaite’s spring 2027 show yesterday, though, felt particularly special. It marked Warner’s first time attending a presentation by the New York label that she has admired for years—and, waiting on the runway, was a familiar face: her The Shards co-star Kaia Gerber, opening the show.
“I haven’t spent much time back in New York [recently], so coming home and being here for NYFW feels full circle,” Warner tells Vogue. “I grew up in this city, so it’s really nice to be back.”

articles.title: 43 Easy 30-Minute Dinner Ideas for Busy Nights
articles.summary: Gochujang chicken, sizzling shrimp, sheet-pan gnocchi, and 40 more ways to get dinner on the table fast.
body: When you need dinner on the table fast, these 30-minute dinner ideas deliver. They’re the recipes Bon Appétit editors turn to when it’s 7 p.m., we’re already hungry, and we haven’t even made it home yet.

But quick doesn’t have to mean boring. These easy 30-minute meals include spicy chicken lettuce wraps, sizzling shrimp fajitas, creamy carbonara, crispy tofu with peanut sauce, and plenty of one-pan dinners that minimize cleanup. Some lean on smart shortcuts like rotisserie chicken, canned tuna, or store-bought dumplings; others take advantage of naturally quick-cooking ingredients like shrimp, ground meat, tofu, and eggs.
Every recipe here can be made in 30 minutes or less, start to finish. Really pressed for time? Our 15-minute meals round-up includes even speedier options.

articles.title: I Tried Rag & Bone’s Viral Sweatpants Jeans—Here’s Why I Love Them for Travel
articles.summary: For the first time in my life, I'm comfortably wearing jeans on the plane.
body: I firmly value comfort over style when it comes to my airport fit, but as I get older and travel more often, I've been on the hunt for a go-to outfit that combines both—seamlessly taking me from long plane rides to walking around a new city with ease. So, when I was flying home from Rome with a friend who was looking particularly fashionable (and to my shock, comfortable ) in jeans, I was convinced on the spot to nab a pair of my own for my next long-haul flight. She was wearing Rag & Bone's sweatpant jeans: The viral pants that look like a structured pair of denim, but feel as soft and stretchy as your favorite pajamas.

I quickly got my hands on Rag & Bone's rb Miramar Shea ankle relaxed straight pant in the color Lakewood, a perfect medium wash. I wanted a pair of travel pants that looked polished enough to wear to check in at a five-star resort but comfy enough to sport on a packed economy flight —and this pair definitely delivers. These soft and stylish sweatpant jeans have become a permanent fixture in my airport uniform, whether I'm hoping on a red-eye or an early morning departure so I can arrive ready for whatever's on the itinerary.

body: A born-and-raised Vancouverite, I’ve spent a lifetime exploring my city’s distinct neighborhoods, and many of my favorite places are found well beyond the downtown core where most of Vancouver’s top hotels are located. Settling into one of the city’s distinct neighborhoods puts the area’s best attractions right outside your door, offering a chance to connect with the surrounding nature, exceptional food scene, and immersive cultural experiences you might otherwise miss. To truly get a taste of all this city has to offer (and experience it like a local), consider booking an Airbnb.

A short-term rental gives you options, whether you want to be steps from sandy Kits Beach, close to the eclectic shops and cafés of Commercial Drive, or tucked away on a leafy residential street in Shaughnessy. For those exploring without a car, many of Vancouver’s neighborhoods are well connected by public transit, too. From a cozy houseboat in the harbor to a light-filled log home on the beach, these are the spots I’d choose for a truly unforgettable stay in the city.
